# Rotterdam depot

The Rotterdam depot opens at 06:00 and closes at 22:00, and its cold room holds 40 pallets held between 2 and 8 °C [src: docs/depots.md]. It is one of the two chilled-goods depots in the network, alongside [Hamburg](hamburg-depot.md), and is the origin or destination of the [Nordfreight](carrier-network.md) chilled lane.

## Cold room and alarm handling

When the cold room passes 8 °C for ten minutes, the shift lead moves the pallets to a backup cold room on site and calls facilities on extension 4410 [src: docs/alarms.md]. Every alarm is logged in the incident book within the hour [src: docs/alarms.md]. The existence of a backup room alongside the 40-pallet main room is stated only in the alarm procedure, so the backup room's capacity is not known *(unverified)*.

## Staffing

Rotterdam runs three shifts, each with a shift lead and six pickers; new pickers shadow an experienced picker for two weeks [src: docs/staff.md]. See [staffing and shifts](../topics/staffing-and-shifts.md) and the [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md).
", "path": "wiki/entities/rotterdam-depot.md"}

# Depot network overview

The network runs four depots: Rotterdam and Hamburg handle chilled goods in cold rooms, Antwerp is dry-goods only with no cold room, and Gdansk is a 2025 addition that also handles dry goods only [src: docs/depots.md].

## Opening times and cold storage

| Depot | Opens | Closes | Cold room |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Rotterdam depot](rotterdam-depot.md) | 06:00 | 22:00 | 40 pallets, 2 to 8 °C |
| [Hamburg depot](hamburg-depot.md) | 05:30 | — | 25 pallets |
| [Antwerp depot](antwerp-depot.md) | 07:00 | — | none |
| [Gdansk depot](gdansk-depot.md) | — | — | dry goods only |

Closing time is given only for Rotterdam (22:00); the other depots' closing hours are not stated in the documents *(unverified)* [src: docs/depots.md].

## Related pages

Cold-room temperature excursions are handled by the [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md). Carriage between the depots is covered by the [carrier network](carrier-network.md), staffing by [staffing and shifts](staffing-and-shifts.md), and goods coming back to the depot that shipped them by [returns handling](../procedures/returns-handling.md).
", "path": "wiki/topics/depot-network.md"}

The Gdansk depot opened in 2025, making it the newest of the four depots, and handles dry goods only [src: docs/depots.md]. Opening hours and any cold storage are not stated *(unverified)*.

[Baltic Reefer](../topics/carrier-network.md) carries chilled goods from [Hamburg](hamburg-depot.md) to Gdansk on Mondays [src: docs/carriers.md]. # Hamburg depot

The Hamburg depot opens at 05:30, the earliest opening in the network, and its cold room holds 25 pallets [src: docs/depots.md]. It handles chilled goods and is the hub between the [Rotterdam](../entities/rotterdam-depot.md) lane and the Baltic lane run by [Baltic Reefer](../topics/carrier-network.md) to [Gdansk](gdansk-depot.md). Closing hours are not given *(unverified)*.

## Night shift and alarm handling

Hamburg's night shift has a night manager instead of a shift lead [src: docs/staff.md]. Unlike Rotterdam's timed escalation, the Hamburg cold-room alarm pages the night manager directly, and the alarm is logged in the incident book within the hour [src: docs/alarms.md]. See [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md).

## Fire drill finding

Hamburg was the depot where the last quarterly fire drill found a blocked exit, since cleared [src: docs/safety.md]. Quarterly drills run at every depot; see [depot safety requirements](../procedures/depot-safety-requirements.md).
", "path": "wiki/entities/hamburg-depot.md"}

# Antwerp depot

The Antwerp depot opens at 07:00, the latest opening in the network, and has no cold room, so it takes no chilled stock [src: docs/depots.md]. Its closing time is not given in the documents *(unverified)*.

## Staffing

Antwerp runs two shifts, fewer than the three at [Rotterdam](rotterdam-depot.md) [src: docs/staff.md]. Because there is no cold room, the [cold-chain alarm](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md) does not apply at Antwerp; chilled returns could not be held there anyway, and returns are inspected at the depot that shipped them [src: docs/returns.md]. See [returns handling](../procedures/returns-handling.md).

# Carrier network

Three carriers move goods between the depots, two of them chilled: Nordfreight, Van Dijk and Baltic Reefer [src: docs/carriers.md]. Every carrier must present a temperature log at hand-over, including the dry-goods operator [src: docs/carriers.md].

## Lanes and schedules

- **Nordfreight** — chilled goods between [Rotterdam](../entities/rotterdam-depot.md) and [Hamburg](../entities/hamburg-depot.md), on Tuesdays and Fridays [src: docs/carriers.md].
- **Van Dijk** — dry goods, running daily; the documents do not name which lanes it serves *(unverified)* [src: docs/carriers.md].
- **Baltic Reefer** — chilled goods from [Hamburg](../entities/hamburg-depot.md) to [Gdansk](../entities/gdansk-depot.md) on Mondays; no return day is stated *(unverified)* [src: docs/carriers.md].

## Chilled flow

Because chilled goods move only on Tuesday, Friday and Monday sailings, a chilled consignment can sit outside a cold room over the weekend gap between Friday and Monday, which is what the [cold-chain alarm](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md) and the 24-hour [returns](../procedures/returns-handling.md) window bear on. The documents do not state transit times, so the size of that gap is not established *(unverified)*.
", "path": "wiki/topics/carrier-network.md"}

See [cold-chain alarm response](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm-response.md).

## Fire drill finding

Hamburg was the depot where the last quarterly fire drill found a blocked exit, since cleared [src: docs/safety.md]. Quarterly drills run at every depot; see [depot safety rules](../procedures/depot-safety-rules.md).
